title: T2 Late Filing Penalty Calculator | Subsection 162(1)
content:
Penalty

T2 Late Filing Penalty Calculator

The late-filing penalty is a percentage of the tax unpaid at the due date, so a return with no tax owing produces no percentage penalty.

5% plus 1% per monthTwelve months maximumA percentage of tax owing$0.00 on a nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your return and what it owed

Enter the year-end, the tax owing and the filing date.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Penalty Is a Percentage, Not a Flat Fee

Subsection 162(1) of the Income Tax Act sets the late-filing penalty at five per cent of the tax that was unpaid when the return came due, plus a further one per cent of that same amount for each complete month the return stays unfiled. The monthly part runs for at most twelve months, which puts the ceiling at seventeen per cent.

Two things follow from the words “of the tax unpaid”. A month that is not yet complete adds nothing, so filing on day twenty-nine of a month costs the same as filing on day one of it. And a return with no tax unpaid has nothing for either percentage to apply to.

What the Same Arithmetic Does to a Nil Year

The yearTax unpaid at the due datePenalty at twelve months
Owed $9,000.00$9,000.00$1,530.00, being 17%
Owed $1,200.00$1,200.00$204.00, being 17%
A true nil year$0.00$0.00, because 17% of nil is nil

That last row is the reason this page exists and also the reason it does not stop there. A nil year carries no percentage penalty and still stays open indefinitely, still invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, and still blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution. The nil return late penalty checker runs that question on its own, and the non-resident T2 penalty calculator covers the one charge that does not depend on tax owing at all.

The percentage needs something to be a percentage of, and that is the whole reason a nil year and a year with tax owing come out so far apart.

Interest Is Separate, and Keeps Running

The penalty and the arrears interest are two charges. The penalty stops growing once twelve complete months have passed; interest on an unpaid balance does not stop until the balance is paid. A nil year has no balance, so it accrues no interest either.

Relief from a penalty already assessed is a separate application again, and the taxpayer relief eligibility checker covers the grounds and the ten-year window. For years still unfiled, nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year closes one tax year per return, and the unfiled years cost calculator totals several at once. The guide to T2 late-filing penalties sets out the provisions in full.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is the T2 late filing penalty?

Five per cent of the tax unpaid at the due date, plus one per cent of that amount for each complete month the return is late, to a maximum of twelve months.

What is the maximum?

Seventeen per cent of the tax that was unpaid at the due date, reached once twelve complete months have gone by.

Is there a penalty if the corporation owes no tax?

The percentage produces $0.00, because there is no unpaid tax for it to apply to. The unfiled year still stays open and still has consequences.

Does a part month count?

No. Only complete months are counted, so the figure steps up on the monthly anniversary of the due date rather than daily.

When is the T2 due?

Within six months of the fiscal year-end. The calculator works the due date out from the year-end you enter.

Does the penalty apply to a return filed on the due date?

No. Subsection 162(1) applies only to a return filed after its due date.

Is this the same as the repeated failure penalty?

No. That is subsection 162(2), at ten per cent plus two per cent per month, and it needs a demand to file and a prior penalty before it applies.

Does interest get added on top?

Arrears interest runs on an unpaid balance separately from the penalty, and unlike the penalty it does not stop at twelve months.

Can the penalty be cancelled?

The Minister may waive or cancel a penalty on specified grounds. That is a taxpayer relief request and it has its own ten-year window.

Will filing late years now make the penalty larger?

No. The monthly part is capped at twelve months and most unfiled years are long past that, so filing stops nothing from growing but closes the year.

title: Repeated Failure to File Penalty Calculator | 162(2)
content:
Penalty

Repeated Failure to File Penalty Calculator

The larger late-filing penalty applies only when a demand to file was served and a penalty was already assessed in one of the three preceding years.

10% plus 2% per monthTwenty months maximumTwo conditions, both required$0.00 on a nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

The year, and what came before it

Enter the two figures and answer the two questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Both Conditions Have to Be Met

Subsection 162(2) is often described as the penalty for filing late again, which understates what it takes to trigger. Two things must both be true of the year in question: the Canada Revenue Agency served a demand to file for it, and a late-filing penalty under subsection 162(1) was assessed for any of the three tax years immediately before it.

Miss either one and the ordinary provision applies instead. A corporation with nine unfiled years and no demand ever served is on 162(1), not this one, however many years have gone by.

Twice the Rate, and Twenty Months Instead of Twelve

Subsection 162(1)Subsection 162(2)
Flat part5% of tax unpaid10% of tax unpaid
Each complete month1%2%
Months counted, at most1220
Ceiling17%50%
Needs a demand to fileNoYes
Needs a prior penaltyNoYes, in the preceding three years

Both are percentages of the tax that was unpaid at the due date, which is the point most easily lost. Fifty per cent of nil is nil, so a corporation whose unfiled years were genuinely nil is not exposed to this figure at all, no matter how many demands arrive. The nil return late penalty checker and the T2 late filing penalty calculator take the same arithmetic from the other two directions.

Two conditions have to be met before this provision applies at all, and most corporations asking about it have met only one.

A Demand Is the Part Worth Acting On

Of the two conditions, only one is still in the corporation’s hands. A penalty assessed in an earlier year is history. A demand to file has a date on it, and filing by that date is what answers it. The demand to file deadline calculator works the date out, and the arbitrary assessment response checker covers what happens when the date goes by.

Where the years are nil, nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year closes one tax year per return and the catch-up filing schedule generator puts several in order, oldest first. The guide to responding to a demand to file covers what a demand asks and what answering it takes.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the repeated failure to file penalty?

Subsection 162(2): ten per cent of the tax unpaid at the due date, plus two per cent of it for each complete month late, to twenty months.

What is the maximum?

Fifty per cent of the tax that was unpaid at the due date, reached at twenty complete months.

When does it apply instead of the ordinary penalty?

Only when a demand to file was served for the year and a late-filing penalty was assessed for one of the three preceding tax years.

I have filed late several years in a row. Does it apply?

Not on its own. Without a demand to file for the year in question, the ordinary five per cent provision applies however many years are late.

Does it apply to a nil return?

The percentage produces $0.00, because there is no unpaid tax. The unfiled year itself still has consequences.

How far back does the prior penalty have to be?

Within the three tax years immediately preceding the year in question.

Does a part month count?

No. Only complete months are counted, on the monthly anniversary of the due date.

What is a demand to file?

A written requirement under subsection 150(2) to file a return, with a date by which it must be filed.

Can both penalties apply to one year?

No. One provision or the other applies to a given tax year, not both.

Can it be cancelled?

It can be the subject of a taxpayer relief request on specified grounds, within the ten-year window that applies to those requests.

title: GST/HST Nil Return Deadline Calculator | When It Is Due
content:
GST/HST

GST/HST Nil Return Deadline Calculator

An open GST/HST account reports every period whether or not anything was collected, on a calendar of its own that the T2 does not touch.

Annual filers, three monthsMonthly and quarterly, one monthA nil return is still a returnSeparate from the T2

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your GST/HST account and its period

Enter the period end and answer the two questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Calendars, Depending on the Filing Frequency

A GST/HST return is due one month after the end of the reporting period for a monthly or quarterly filer, and three months after the fiscal year end for an annual filer. A corporation that registered once and never looked again is almost always an annual filer, because that is the default at low revenue.

Neither date has anything to do with the six months that governs the T2. A December 31 year-end puts the T2 at June 30 and an annual GST/HST return at March 31, so the two land in different quarters and are missed independently of each other.

A Period With No Activity Is Still a Period

Filing frequencyPeriod endingReturn due
AnnualDecember 31March 31
AnnualJune 30September 30
QuarterlyMarch 31April 30
MonthlyJanuary 31February 28 or 29

An account that collected nothing files a nil return rather than nothing at all, and the obligation runs from the registration, not from the activity. That is why a dormant corporation can be perfectly correct on its T2 and still be behind on a second account nobody closed. The GST/HST nil filing checker decides whether the account needs returns, and the GST/HST account closure checker covers form RC145 and what closing one takes.

An account that was opened and never closed keeps its own filing calendar, and that calendar has nothing to do with the T2.

What the Nil T2 Fee Does and Does Not Reach

Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year is the federal corporate income tax return, transmitted electronically. The GST/HST account is a separate registration with its own returns, its own periods and its own exposure, and filing it is not part of that fee. We will tell you the date; the return against that account stays yours to file or to close.

Where several accounts are being wound down at once, the order matters, and the CRA account closure sequencer sets it out. For the corporate return itself the next T2 due date checker gives the date on the other calendar, and the guide to CRA accounts on a dormant corporation covers every account a quiet corporation still carries.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is a nil GST/HST return due?

One month after the end of the reporting period for a monthly or quarterly filer, and three months after the fiscal year end for an annual filer.

Does a dormant corporation have to file GST/HST returns?

If the account is still open, yes. The obligation follows the registration rather than the activity.

Is a nil return the same as not filing?

No. A nil return reports that the period had nothing in it. Not filing leaves the period unreported.

Is it due at the same time as the T2?

No. The T2 runs six months from the fiscal year-end; neither GST/HST date does.

How do I know whether the account files annually?

The Canada Revenue Agency assigns the frequency, and annual is the default at low revenue. The confirmation of registration states it.

Is the GST/HST return included in the nil T2 fee?

No. The fee covers the federal corporate income tax return. The GST/HST account is a separate registration.

What if the account should have been closed years ago?

The periods between then and now are still reportable until it is closed. Closing it takes a final return and form RC145.

Is there a penalty on a nil GST/HST return filed late?

The failure-to-file penalty is calculated on an amount owing, so a nil period produces no percentage charge. The period stays unreported until it is filed.

Does the due date shift off a weekend?

The Canada Revenue Agency treats a payment or return received on the next business day as on time when the due date falls on a weekend or a holiday.

Can one return cover several missed periods?

No. Each reporting period is its own return, in the same way each tax year is its own T2.

title: Voluntary Disclosure Eligibility Checker | CRA VDP
content:
Catch-Up

Voluntary Disclosure Eligibility Checker

The programme relieves penalties on a disclosure made before the Canada Revenue Agency acts, which is why a nil year rarely needs it.

Voluntary, before the Agency actsOne year past dueComplete, or not at allNil years rarely need it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your unfiled years

Answer the four questions and the conditions are set out here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What the Programme Requires

The Voluntary Disclosures Programme lets a taxpayer correct an earlier filing position and have penalties relieved. Four things are asked of an application: that it be voluntary, meaning made before the Canada Revenue Agency takes enforcement action on the matter; that it be complete; that it involve the application of a penalty; and that it include information at least one year past due.

The first is the one that closes the door. A letter, a telephone call or a demand to file about the years in question generally ends the possibility of a voluntary disclosure about them, which is why the programme is of no use to someone who waited for contact.

Why a Nil Year Usually Does Not Need It

A year with tax owingA true nil year
Late-filing penaltyUp to 17% of the tax unpaid$0.00
Arrears interestRuns until the balance is paidNone
What the programme relievesThe penalty and part of the interestNothing, because there is neither
The practical routeConsider an applicationFile the years

The programme relieves penalties. Where the unfiled years were genuinely nil there is no percentage penalty and no interest, so an application spends time and professional fees to relieve charges that were never assessed. Filing the years is the shorter route, and the nil return late penalty checker sets out what the open years do cost instead.

The programme exists to relieve penalties, so a year that was charged none of them has nothing for it to relieve.

If the Years Were Not Nil

A corporation with unreported income, a dividend paid or received, rent collected or investment income in any of the years is not filing nil returns, and the calculation above does not apply to it. Those years carry real tax, real penalties and real interest, and an application may be worth making.

That work is not what this site does. It is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus applicable sales tax per year, and a disclosure is a matter to take advice on before filing anything. Where the years are nil, nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year closes one per return and the catch-up filing schedule generator orders them. The guide to catching up unfiled corporate tax returns is the longer treatment.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Voluntary Disclosures Programme?

A Canada Revenue Agency programme that relieves penalties, and part of the interest, on a disclosure a taxpayer makes before the Agency acts.

What makes a disclosure voluntary?

That it is made before the Agency takes enforcement action on the matter. Contact about the years in question generally ends it.

How overdue does something have to be?

The application must include information at least one year past its due date.

Can I disclose some years and not others?

No. The programme requires a complete disclosure, and a partial one fails that condition.

Do nil years need a voluntary disclosure?

Usually not. The programme relieves penalties, and a true nil year carries no percentage penalty and no interest for it to relieve.

Does an application stop a demand to file?

No. A demand has its own date, and filing by that date is what answers it.

Does meeting the conditions assure relief?

No. An application is assessed on its facts and may be accepted into either of the programme tracks, or refused.

Is the tax itself forgiven?

No. The estimated tax owing is paid with the application. The relief is from penalties and part of the interest.

How many years back can a disclosure go?

There is no fixed limit on the years disclosed, though interest relief is bounded by its own ten-year rule.

What is the difference from taxpayer relief?

A disclosure corrects a filing position before the Agency acts. Taxpayer relief asks the Minister to cancel charges already assessed.

title: Taxpayer Relief Eligibility Checker | Ten-Year Window
content:
Relief

Taxpayer Relief Eligibility Checker

The Minister may cancel penalties and interest on specified grounds, but only for a tax year inside the ten-year window.

Ten-year windowPenalties and interest onlyDiscretionary, on groundsForm RC4288

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

The year and the grounds

Enter the year and answer the three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Ten-Year Window Is the First Test

Subsection 220(3.1) of the Income Tax Act lets the Minister waive or cancel a penalty or interest. The discretion is bounded: a request may only reach a tax year that ended within the ten calendar years before the calendar year in which the request is made. A request made during 2026 therefore reaches tax years ending in 2016 or later.

The window moves every January, which cuts both ways: waiting a year to ask does not improve a request and can put the oldest year it covers permanently out of reach.

It Cancels Charges, Not Tax

What was assessedCan relief reach it
Late-filing penaltyYes, on grounds and inside the window
Arrears interestYes, on the same basis
The tax itselfNo. Relief never touches the tax
A charge on a nil yearThere is none to reach

That last row is where most corporate enquiries about relief actually land. A true nil year carried no percentage penalty and no interest, so a request has nothing to cancel, and the thing that closes the year is the return. The T2 late filing penalty calculator shows the arithmetic that produces $0.00, and the nil return late penalty checker sets out what an open year costs instead of a percentage.

Relief reaches the penalty and the interest, never the tax, and on a nil year there was never any of the three.

The Grounds, and the Order of Operations

Three groups of circumstances are recognised: extraordinary circumstances outside the taxpayer’s control, such as a natural disaster, a serious illness or a death; actions of the Canada Revenue Agency itself, such as processing delays or incorrect information; and an inability to pay or financial hardship. Form RC4288 is the request, and it is decided case by case.

Outstanding returns are filed before the request or with it. Asking for charges to be cancelled on a year that has not been filed leaves the year open, so nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year or the catch-up filing schedule generator comes first. A correction made before the Agency acts is a different route again, and the voluntary disclosure eligibility checker covers it. The guide to corporate tax arrears and interest covers what the charges are before any request to cancel them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is taxpayer relief?

A discretionary cancellation or waiver of penalties and interest by the Minister under subsection 220(3.1) of the Income Tax Act.

How far back can a request go?

To a tax year that ended within the ten calendar years before the calendar year the request is made in.

Can relief cancel the tax owing?

No. It reaches penalties and interest only. The tax itself stands.

What grounds are recognised?

Extraordinary circumstances outside your control, actions of the Canada Revenue Agency, and an inability to pay or financial hardship.

Which form is used?

Form RC4288, the request for taxpayer relief.

Is relief automatic once a ground applies?

No. It is discretionary and each request is decided on its own facts.

Does a nil year qualify for relief?

There is nothing to relieve. A true nil year carries no percentage penalty and no interest, so filing the return is what resolves it.

Do the returns have to be filed first?

They are normally filed before the request or with it. An unfiled year stays open regardless of the request.

Is this the same as a voluntary disclosure?

No. A disclosure corrects a position before the Agency acts; relief asks for charges already assessed to be cancelled.

Does the window move?

Yes, every calendar year, so the oldest year a request can reach moves forward each January.
